text:
ajenkins: Quick heads-up — product is planning a staged rollout next Tue in EU-North and APAC. Early forecast shows a 15-25% bump in concurrent chat sessions, rough extra 400-550 GPU-hours/day for first 48h. Can infra eyeball headroom?

maria_g: noted. On the cushion report I saw eu-north at ~8% spare throughput yesterday at peak (incl. autoscale buffers). APAC is tighter at ~3%. :grimacing:

kai_chen: do we have tokens/sec projections for the staged rollout traffic profile? synchronous chat vs. streaming matters a lot for GPU time.

ajenkins: marketing gave a routing split: 60% eu, 30% apac, 10% us. They expect avg session length +25% due to longer prompts. Quick WAG: +20% tokens/sec in eu.

luis: infra-bot logs show recent node churn in eu-north after the kernel update — ~2 nodes in rack-4 flapping last 72h. Might reduce effective capacity by ~6%.

infra-bot: [alert] 1850029001 autoscaler: scale-down aborted due to pending evictions; evictions=4, reason=noisy-neighbor 

sre_oncall: logs also show inter-AZ NIC errors around 03:10 UTC yesterday for eu-north. Packets dropped -> retransmits -> tail latency spikes. Filing a network ticket.

maria_g: we should factor warmup waste into headroom calc. For chat models we see ~8-12% warmup token overhead on cold peers.

ajenkins: Agreed. Quick calc to illustrate gap: 
```
peak_tokens_per_sec = 210000
avg_tokens_per_sec = 130000
tokens_per_gpu_sec = 640  # measured for this model at seq=1024 on A100-80GB
needed_gpus_peak = ceil(peak_tokens_per_sec / tokens_per_gpu_sec) = 329
current_pool_eu = 300
effective_pool_after_flap = current_pool_eu * 0.94 = 282
headroom = effective_pool_after_flap - needed_gpus_peak = -47 (short)
warmup_overhead = 0.10 -> additional ~33 GPUs
net_shortfall = -80 GPUs
```

kai_chen: yikes. If that calc is close, we need either temporary burst seats (dedicated) or re-route percentage to us while we stabilize. What's cost delta for burst vs manual re-route?

luis: rough numbers: burst rented GPUs for 48h ~ $35k; re-route penalty (added latency + RU) ~= $4k revenue risk estimate for 48h plus operational cost. Burst likely cheaper if SLA violations matter.

sre_oncall: alternative: small config change — decrease max batch size by 1 and increase token-level concurrency to trade throughput for latency headroom. Could shave 12-15% GPU usage for chat but increases p50 slightly. Want to test canary?

maria_g: let's canary that in eu-north with 5% traffic and instrument tokens/sec and p95 latency. If delta holds, we can roll to 30% and free up pool.

ajenkins: plan proposal: 1) Canary batch-size tweak (5% eu) for 3h; 2) If p95 < 400ms, roll to 30% and request 24h burst capacity for APAC only; 3) open network ticket + schedule emergency kernel rollback window if node flapping persists.

kai_chen: I'll run a simulation with our traffic replay (include warmup) and post updated headroom numbers within 2h.

luis: I'll prep cost request for burst seats and ping sales for temporary reservation (fast approval path).

sre_oncall: created ticket NET-4521 for eu-north AZ NIC errors and root cause triage.

ajenkins: thanks everyone. Post results here. If simulation still shows >50 GPU shortfall, we'll approve burst. @maria_g tag with the canary run config when ready. :thumbsup:
